note: Genre-pack-owned cue event map for the 3D top-down extraction-shooter / greed-loop quadrant (SFX dogfood learnings; backlog High #5). Seeded from the Extraction/Roguelike/Top-Down taxonomy: required cues = fire, hit, hurt, loot open, loot tier reward, extract start/complete, enemy death, player death; optional cues = danger escalation, stash/bank, low health, zone warning. Each cue declares its game-event binding, layer roles, frequency class, variant/anti-fatigue policy, priority, mixer bus, and spatial policy — SFX as a semantic system, not a file drop. This is the DECLARATION the SFX gates read; it does not itself bind clips (that is the build stage's asset-binding capture).

honestyRules.rule: A cue's grammar names the PHYSICAL ACTION first, not a mood word: `metal footlocker clasp flips open, then a small reward bell` — not `loot pickup chime`. The dogfood project's first loot cue read as a swing/woosh because it was prompted for mood; the fix was changing the sound grammar to physical-action-first.

A cue with frequency `frequent` MUST carry a variantPolicy with count >= 2 and noImmediateRepeat:true (plus pitch/volume jitter). The dogfood project added round-robin/no-repeat variants for fire/hit/hurt/enemy-death precisely because single-clip frequent cues fatigue fast.

A tiered/parametrized cue maps an event PAYLOAD field to its variant/tier (loot_reward reads `lootTier`); never a global PlayLoot() that hides the game state needed for better feedback. Tiered loot worked in the dogfood project because LootContainer already emitted the looted value.

A critical/accessibility cue (low_health, zone_warning, player_death) must ALSO be represented visually or via captions — never make audio the only channel for critical information (Game Accessibility Guidelines / Xbox AG 104).

cues.meaning: Player fired the weapon — the primary input confirm; latency-sensitive. Self-feedback stays 2D for immediacy. transient = timing readability, body = weapon weight/identity, sweetener = mechanical click.
Player shot connected with an enemy — the hit-confirm. Positional (3D) so world threats read by direction; distinct from `fire` and from `enemy_death`.
Player took damage — self-feedback pain cue, 2D for immediacy.
Physical action of opening a loot container: the metal footlocker clasp flips open. Shared identity across tiers; the reward chime is the separate `loot_reward` cue.

The reward confirm after the clasp: a small bell/chime whose richness escalates by loot tier (low/mid/high share the clasp identity, then add richer reward tails). Tier read from the telemetry `loot_complete` event's `tier` payload (ground-truthed real tiers low/mid/high) — not a global chime. Event name matches the telemetry event type so cue fires can be cross-verified against the run's event stream.
Player began the extraction hold — high priority so it cuts through combat; marks the greed-vs-safety decision point.
Extraction completed and value is banked — the run-secured relief/reward payoff.
An enemy was killed — positional world event, distinct from the `hit` confirm.
Player died and forfeited carried value — the run-lost failure cue. Also represented visually (see audio-not-sole-channel).
Optional risk-escalation stinger as heat/danger rises — a greed-arc mood layer on the music bus.
Optional stash/bank deposit confirm on the UI bus.
Optional low-health warning state. Accessibility: must pair with a visual equivalent (audio-not-sole-channel).
Optional zone/collapse warning — positional so it doubles as spatial guidance toward/away from the hazard.
